etymologies.heading: Etymology
paragraphs: Learned borrowing from Late Latin exēgēsĭs (“exposition”), or from its etymon Ancient Greek ἐξήγησῐς (exḗgēsĭs, “explanation, interpretation; narration”), from ἐξηγέομαι (exēgéomai, “to guide, lead; to expound, interpret; to explain, relate”) + -σῐς (-sĭs, suffix forming abstract nouns or nouns of action, process, or result). Ἐξηγέομαι (Exēgéomai) is derived from ἐξ- (ex-) (a variant of ἐκ- (ek-, prefix meaning ‘away; off; out’)) + ἡγέομαι (hēgéomai, “to guide, lead”) (possibly ultimately from Proto-Indo-European *h₂eǵ- (“to drive”) or *seh₂g- (“to follow; to seek out, trace”)).
The plural form is a learned borrowing from Late Latin exēgēsēs or its etymon Ancient Greek ἐξηγήσεις (exēgḗseis).
senses: (mathematics, historical) In full numeral exegesis: a procedure formerly used to solve algebraic equations.
